claim: The medium the background painting is made in, which is a separate axis from how finished it is and is what actually makes a film look painted rather than rendered. Watercolour reads gentle and hand-made; photobash reads modern, cheap and slightly uncanny against 2D characters.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: flat cel background, flat color scenery
poster color background, opaque flat painted scenery
gouache (medium) background, opaque matte painted scenery
acrylic paint (medium) background, matte painted scenery
digital painted background, detailed painted scenery
line and wash background, ink lines with watercolor scenery
graphic flat background, minimalist vector scenery, flat color shapes

review.issue: poster_color ("opaque flat painted scenery"), gouache ("opaque matte painted scenery") and acrylic_matte ("matte painted scenery") differ only by a medium name the model has weak signal for plus the same two adjectives; they will render as one picture three times. digital_painted vs photoreal_painted vs photobash sit similarly close at the other end. Twelve options is also well past what this axis can actually resolve.
review.fix: Collapse to the mediums Animagine genuinely distinguishes: cel_flat, watercolor, gouache (keep one of the opaque-paint three), airbrush_soft, digital_painted, photobash, ukiyo_e, graphic_flat. Use the bare danbooru medium tag as the anchor - "gouache (medium)", "watercolor (medium)" - and drop the descriptive tails.

look_at: ukiyo_e/graphic_flat/watercolor unmistakable; half the media are interchangeable; style takes the character with it.
